A self-blind-solve by this auditor would therefore be contaminated and is NOT offered as evidence. Three independent uncontaminated reads were commissioned instead, each given only the material named in its brief, with no key, no rationale, no generator_meta, no gate history and no web access.

independent_read_1.role: skeptical test-wise cold solver, passage + stem + options only
independent_read_1.jointly_defensible_pair: A+D flagged as the one pair where a case exists for both, then resolved against A: 'D would explain A', but A is rejected because 'in order to' imports intention the passage never records and the bookseller's two o'clock start is direct counter-evidence to a claim about 'the keepers'.
independent_read_1.decisive_evidence_cited: 'the chandler's hatch opened at seven in the morning and took in 412 letters; the bookseller's opened at two and took in 390' set against 'Both shut when the evening cart went at eight.' - identified as the sentence that converts the figures into an inference.
independent_read_1.arithmetic_reproduced_independently: 13 h vs 6 h; 412 - 390 = 22 letters = 5.64% more post for 117% more opening; marginal 3.1 letters/hour on the chandler's extra seven hours against the bookseller's 65.0 letters/hour; allowance 39d (3s 3d) vs 18d (1s 6d) per day.
independent_read_1.self_reported_friction_against_the_key: 'Governed' does more work than the passage licenses; the negative half (length of opening does not predict volume) is firm, the positive half (the cart's hour is the governing variable) is reconstruction. Also n=2, one quarter, no control, and the chandler did still take 22 more, so D's 'not' is absolute where the data are merely lopsided.
independent_read_1.blind_channel_reported_unprompted: Asked separately for a no-passage pick, this solver also returned D at medium-high confidence and volunteered: 'That convergence is the finding: a test-wise reader can reach the key without the passage.'

independent_read_2.role: adversarial counsel instructed to build the strongest case for A, then C, then B, then attack D, then rule as judge
independent_read_2.best_move_found_for_A: Counsel's strongest construction: 'the keepers' need not be distributive - English readily takes a definite plural as a class or office statement, so one documented stretcher instantiates the practice; and 'stretched' has an implicit baseline in the traffic itself (six hours captures 390 letters, so anything beyond the traffic's requirement is stretch), on which the bookseller is not a counterexample but merely a keeper who stretched less. Supporting exhibits: the gratuitous clause 'and not a penny for the letters themselves', which exists only to make the reader act on the incentive; 'The quarterly returns recorded the hours', making hours the claimable, auditable, remunerated quantity; and a marginal return of about three letters per hour on the chandler's morning against a fixed 3d an hour that does not depend on anything coming through the hatch.
independent_read_2.why_A_still_dies: Three defeats. (i) 'in order to' is a purpose claim and the passage records not a syllable of anyone's intention - incentive plus consistent behaviour is the SHAPE of a motive hypothesis, not evidence for one. (ii) The bookseller is worse for A than counsel admits: he declines seven hours of guaranteed money every day for a whole quarter, so he is not a lesser stretcher but an anomaly, and he is 50% of the evidence; the passage supplies its own control condition and A fails it. (iii) The surveyor is the audit function, sees the returns of hours AND letters, and 'remarked only that the chandler's flap wanted a new spring' - the word 'only' is deliberate, and the one person positioned to call the hours excessive raises nothing. A reads a scandal into a document whose own inspector found none.
independent_read_2.why_C_dies: 'Both shut when the evening cart went at eight.' - both, and at the cart's departure, by explicit statement. The only escapes (hatch shut vs shop shut; a loose temporal 'when') fail because the sentence's whole grammatical purpose is to fix the closing time as a shared constant. C is a half-true premise (390 against 412 IS making up much of a seven-hour deficit) bolted to a mechanism the text refutes in one clause.
independent_read_2.why_B_dies: Direction right, magnitude false: 22 letters is 5.6% against opening hours differing by 117%. 'Far more' asserts precisely the proportionality the figures were built to refute.
independent_read_2.strongest_attack_found_on_D: Four, all recorded and none fatal: (i) 'governed' is a causal verb the text does not earn - what is licensed cleanly is the negative; (ii) the cart's hour is a CONSTANT across both houses, so on n=2 nothing in this evidence could distinguish 'the cart governs volume' from 'the cart is irrelevant and something else produces near-parity' - D's affirmative half is strictly untestable on the data given; (iii) D is phrased as a standing law ('how many letters a hatch took', any hatch) from a single Michaelmas return; (iv) the passage dangles live rivals D forecloses - two different trades with different footfall rhythms, and 'the chandler's flap wanted a new spring', a stiff hatch across a whole quarter being a plausible mechanical depressant on the chandler's count.

independent_read_3.role: pure blind solver - stem and four options only, NO passage, instructed to use surface heuristics and report calibrated probabilities
independent_read_3.structure_found: 3-versus-1 on the causal premise 'opening length drives intake': B asserts it, C presupposes it, D is the sole denier, A is neutral on it. 'When three options live inside a premise and one adjudicates it, the adjudicator is usually the key.' Reported as worth roughly D-60 on its own.
independent_read_3.other_heuristics_that_fired: 'X, not Y' adjudicating shape (unique to D, named as the single strongest signal); stem-type match (A/B/C are reportable facts, D is the mechanism generalisation an 'implied' stem rewards); odd-one-out on subject type (A/B/C take a human or commercial agent, D an abstract constraint); magnitude tell against B ('far more'); motive-attribution tell against A; internal incoherence against C. Option length and parallelism returned NO signal.
independent_read_3.explicit_refusal_to_call_it_random: 'This is not near-random for a blind solver, and I won't report 25/25/25/25. The sheet leaks through construction ... A test-wise student reaches D without the passage.'
independent_read_3.caveat_recorded: Held at 62 rather than 80 because the 'X, not Y' frame is occasionally built inverted as bait, and because a loosely worded stem could make B a stated-fact key.

cold_solve.auditors_own_adjudication: Key D CONFIRMED and uniquely defensible. Three independent reads converge on D; the adversarial counsel, given every incentive to break it, rules the item single-answerable and puts A no higher than ARGUABLE, exactly where two G-DISTRACTOR rounds put it. No jointly defensible pair survives scrutiny: the A+D pair read_1 raised is a compatibility relation, not a joint answerability - A can be true alongside D without being IMPLIED by the passage, and 'in order to' is the word that keeps it off the ballot. a_case_ruling.question: Duty 1 - build option A's best case independently and rule honestly. Recorded closest call: A (hourly-allowance incentive), ARGUABLE per G-DISTRACTOR r1 and r2, dying on the bookseller's short hours plus unstated motive.
a_case_ruling.strongest_case_this_audit_could_build: A's case is better than the two G-DISTRACTOR notes give it credit for, because both of them lean on the plural 'the keepers' and that plank is soft. Definite plurals in English routinely name a practice rather than an audited set ('the keepers were allowed threepence' two sentences earlier is itself generic), so 'the keepers stretched their opening hours' can be read as a claim about how the office behaved, which one documented instance instantiates. On that reading the bookseller is not a counterexample but a keeper who stretched less - both exceed what the traffic required, differing only in degree. The passage also front-loads the incentive with a clause that has no other function ('and not a penny for the letters themselves'), then certifies the paper trail ('The quarterly returns recorded the hours and the letters'), then supplies exactly the marginal-return figure that makes padding legible: seven extra hours for twenty-two letters, at threepence an hour that arrives whether or not the hatch is used.
a_case_ruling.ruling: A is ARGUABLE and NOT DEFENSIBLE. The plural reading survives; the motive does not. 'In order to' is a claim about purpose, and the passage contains no purposes at all - no keeper is said to intend, prefer, calculate or notice anything. Incentive plus consistent behaviour is the shape of a motive hypothesis, not evidence for one, and an 'implied' stem in this corpus licenses the best-supported reading of the evidence, not the most cynical reading of the incentives. The generic-plural rescue also costs A its second half: once 'the keepers' names the office rather than the pair, the option stops being about these two receiving houses, which is what the stem asks about. And the passage supplies its own control - a keeper who declines seven hours of guaranteed money every day for a quarter - together with an audit function that looked at both columns and remarked only on a flap spring. Ruled identically by the independent adversarial counsel, unprompted. The two G-DISTRACTOR rounds' disposition is UPHELD, with the note that their stated defeater (the plural) is the weaker of the two available and 'in order to' is the one that actually kills it.
a_case_ruling.prediction_for_field_data: If this item misbehaves in field statistics, A will be why. It is a well-built high-attraction distractor and its refutation is one inferential step subtler than the two the other distractors need.

findings.stage_challenged: blind solvability / G-STEM standing major / the fleet-repair-1 change itself
findings.claim: The post-repair option set is reachable at 62% without the passage, against a 25% floor, and the leak points AT THE KEY. The fleet-repair-1 change that produced this set was made to close a blind channel and made it worse: it traded a two-option contradictory pair (a 1-in-2 channel) for a three-against-one shared-premise cluster that an independent blind solver resolves to the key at 62%. This is the item's principal defect and it is the only finding on which reasonable adjudicators could differ about shipping.
findings.evidence: An uncontaminated blind solver commissioned by this audit was given the stem and the four options with NO passage, no key, no rationale and no gate history, and asked for a calibrated distribution. It returned A 9 / B 13 / C 16 / D 62, refused to call the sheet random ('This is not near-random for a blind solver, and I won't report 25/25/25/25. The sheet leaks through construction ... A test-wise student reaches D without the passage'), and identified the mechanism precisely: 'The sheet is a 3-versus-1 on the causal premise opening length drives intake: B asserts it outright, C presupposes it, A is neutral on it ... D is the sole denier. Under standard construction, the option that names and rejects the premise the others rest on is the key.' It scored that structure alone at roughly D-60. Independently, the passage-based cold solver, asked separately for a no-passage pick, ALSO returned D and volunteered 'That convergence is the finding: a test-wise reader can reach the key without the passage.' Both G-STEM rounds had already found this: r1 'BLIND: PARTIALLY, pick=D ... D is then the only option that names both candidate causes and adjudicates between them - the shape an author writes for a key'; r2, on the repaired sheet, 'the round-1 axis fix did land ... but it also put a second option onto the premise D negates, sharpening rather than softening the blind lean. This is the repair trading an axis imbalance for a shared-presupposition cluster.'
findings.why: Two things make this more than the usual PARTIALLY note. (i) It breaches the batch's own declared line. The efterhandstillagg adopted after batch17 and inherited by batch19 tolerates a structural blind channel only where 'the adversarial blind floor is stated explicitly and is no better than 1-in-2'. 62% is better than 1-in-2. The rule is scoped in terms to stance-composition skew in single-author opinion passages and does not literally govern a history essay with one question, so this is an analogical breach of the bank's stated tolerance rather than a rule violation - which is exactly why it belongs with the owner rather than with a gate. (ii) The lean points at the KEY, not at a distractor. The comparable batch18 finding recorded a residual channel that 'halves the field to 1-in-2, does not resolve, and tips toward a distractor'; that costs a test-wise student nothing. This one hands one. On a one-question unit the whole of the item's discrimination is at stake. AGAINST refuting: the key is right and uniquely defensible on three independent reads; both G-STEM rounds saw this and declined the kill on the ground that all four options remain rescuable by a passage; the 'X, not Y' surface shape is provably NOT an HP key tell (measured here at 0.74% of authentic keys against 0.68% of authentic distractors, i.e. no signal), so the leak runs through the shared-premise structure and through an LLM-flavoured heuristic rather than through anything a Swedish 18-year-old is trained on; and the repair history demonstrates that this defect MOVES rather than resolves - r1's fix created r2's finding, and a third pass would most likely relocate it again while risking A's promotion to DEFENSIBLE, which the repairer correctly refused to gamble on. DISPOSITION: not a refutation, but the owner should rule on ship-as-is versus a structural rewrite, because the cheap repairs available all cost something the unit currently has. Stripping the corrective frame from D ('The cart's hour governed how many letters a hatch took') removes the surface tell and leaves the 3-vs-1 structure intact; putting a second option on the adjudicating shape restores option balance but requires touching A, which G-DISTRACTOR has twice found ARGUABLE and which the repairer deliberately left alone; rewriting C off the premise reinstates the round-1 off-axis defect. The honest options are ship with the channel disclosed, or retire the item.

findings.evidence: gen-elf-short-2.NOTES.md, verbatim: 'Adversarial blind floor (stem + options, no passage): stated explicitly - no better than 1 in 4 by content, and no better than 1 in 2 on any surface heuristic I could construct (three of the four options are contrastive "X rather than Y" claims; the odd one out, B, is a comparative, and it is a distractor, so "pick the odd shape" scores zero).' findings.claim: originality_note certifies that the nearest real places to the invented toponym 'Draystow' are 'each at edit distance 4'. Two real English place names sit at Levenshtein distance 2, and one of them is a market town - the exact category the passage invents Draystow to be. The rule-14 test that BLOCKS (exact bearer, one-letter variant) still passes, so this is a false disclosure and not a collision.
findings.evidence: originality_note, verbatim: '"Draystow" no exact bearer; the nearest real places surfaced are Drayford (Devon), Draycote (Warwickshire), Draycott (Worcestershire) and Draycott in the Clay (Staffordshire), each at edit distance 4 from Draystow, none a one-letter variant.' Levenshtein computed by this audit: Drayford 4, Draycote 4, Draycott 4, 'Draycott in the Clay' 15 - the four listed distances are individually correct. But Drayton = 2 (Draystow -> delete 's' -> Draytow -> substitute w/n -> Drayton) and Bradstow = 2 (substitutions at positions 1 and 4). Existence verified on independent legs with passing controls: en.wikipedia CirrusSearch '"Market Drayton"' -> totalhits 845, top hit 'Market Drayton', 'a market town and civil parish on the banks of the River Tern in Shropshire, England'; '"Bradstow"' -> totalhits 6, the Broadstairs article recording 'at what was then called Bradstow(e), meaning broad place' and the 1958 Birthday Honours recording 'Bradstow Special Educational Needs School, Broadstairs, Kent'. The Drayton family is not obscure and is not hard to surface: Wikipedia's own fuzzy leg, run by this audit as 'Draystow~', returns Market Drayton, West Drayton, Drayton Arms, Drayton Park railway station and Drayton Valley at totalhits 10129.
findings.why: Rule 14 blocks on exact bearers and on one-letter variants, and neither is breached: no exact bearer on any of the three legs with controls passing, and no real place at distance 1. The name is CLEAR to ship on the rule's own terms, and this audit does not escalate it. What is wrong is the disclosure, and this is the SECOND CONSECUTIVE BATCH in which V-FINAL has had to correct an originality_note's neighbour-distance arithmetic in this lane: batch18's elf-b18-004 certified that no real place sat one letter from 'Stintbury' while naming Saintbury - a real Gloucestershire village at distance exactly 1 - among the neighbours it cleared. The pattern is the same (exact legs run properly, neighbour set enumerated from the search results only, distances asserted without being computed) and the failure mode is the same (the note's search surfaced a Dray- cluster and the generator measured the wrong members of it). One batch later, at distance 2 instead of 1, the defect is milder but the process gap is identical and has not been closed. Domain proximity is worth naming: Market Drayton is a Shropshire market town and this passage's opening move is to establish Draystow as an English market town with a market place at its centre. Minimum repair: correct the sentence in originality_note to disclose the distance-2 neighbours honestly. No rename is indicated.

findings.claim: generator_meta.residue_note declares 'the two shops facing each other across the market place' to be concrete residue the question does not test, and the rationale then makes that same fact documented-fact (iv) in the four-fact chain on which the key rests. This is the THIRD CONSECUTIVE BATCH in which V-FINAL has charged this lane with the identical contradiction.
findings.evidence: residue_note, verbatim: 'Concrete residue the question does not test: the hatch cut beside the shop door, the phrase "not a penny for the letters themselves", the two shops facing each other across the market place, Michaelmas as the quarter, and the closing sentence ...'. Rationale, verbatim: 'The documented facts are: ... (iv) the two shops faced each other across the same market place, so they drew on one town and one trading day.' The comparability warrant that (iv) supplies is load-bearing and was recognised as such by an independent reader: the cold solver named it unprompted as 'a nice piece of passage design - the two shops faced each other across the market place, which controls for catchment and footfall, so the difference really is about time rather than place'. Prior charges: batches/batch17/audits/elf-b17-004.json finding 1 ('residue_note contradicts the Q1 rationale: two details it declares to be untested concrete residue are the rationale's own explicit defeaters for distractors B and D'); batches/batch18/audits/elf-b18-004.json INT-1 ('the free benches and the three surnames in pew 9 ... declared untested and used as defeaters'), which itself recorded that the batch17 finding 'was not fed back into the generator brief'.
findings.why: residue_note exists to evidence law 9 - the passage must not resolve into a parable in which every clause serves the answer - and its value depends entirely on the list being honest. Once the market place is subtracted, the genuinely untested residue reduces to the hatch cut beside the shop door, the 'not a penny' phrase, Michaelmas as the quarter and the flap-spring coda. Law 9 still holds comfortably; that residue is real, non-zero and better than most in the lane. But the declared slack overstates the actual slack by one item, and the recurrence is the point: three consecutive batches, three audits, same defect, no feedback path. Milder than its two predecessors, which each miscounted two items. Metadata-only, not student-facing, does not move the verdict. Cheap repair: strike the market-place clause from residue_note. Structural repair: the generator brief needs a rule that residue_note is written AFTER the rationale and screened against it.

findings.claim: The rationale asserts as a documented fact something that is an inference requiring an unstated comparability assumption, in the sentence that carries the key's positive half.
findings.evidence: Rationale, verbatim: 'Seven extra hours of opening bought about twenty-two extra letters, while the six hours the two shops shared carried nearly four hundred at each counter.' The first clause is arithmetic on stated figures and is exact. The second is true by construction for the bookseller (390 letters in exactly those six hours, since he was open at no other time) and INFERRED for the chandler: the passage never says how the chandler's 412 distributed across his thirteen hours. To get 'nearly four hundred' at the chandler's counter in the shared window one must assume the two counters ran at comparable rates in that window - which is what makes the extra-morning-hours yield small. The assumption is well warranted by the passage ('faced each other across the market place'), but it is an assumption, and the sentence states it flat.
findings.why: The rationale is the teaching payload a learner reads after answering, and its job here is to model exactly the one-inch inference the item is built on. Presenting the inferred half as a read-off datum teaches a learner to skip the step the item exists to train. Held at minor because the inference is sound, the warrant is in the passage, and the key is reachable without this sentence at all - both independent reads reached D by the difference alone, without asserting anything about the chandler's within-day distribution. Cheap repair, rationale-only: 'while the bookseller took nearly four hundred in the six hours the two shops shared, and the chandler's morning can therefore have carried very few'.

findings.claim: The key's causal verb 'governed' claims more than the evidence in the passage can carry, and the affirmative half of D is strictly untestable on the data given. Both independent reads raised this without prompting and neither was told the key.
findings.evidence: Cold solver, unprompted, under 'friction with my own answer': 'Governed is doing more work than the passage licenses. What the text firmly supports is the negative half - length of opening does not predict volume. The positive half, that the cart's hour is the governing variable, is my reconstruction of why; the passage never says when within each window the letters actually arrived ... It is one quarter and two houses - n=2, no trend, no control quarter. The chandler did still take more (22 letters), so opening length is not wholly inert; D's not is absolute where the data are merely lopsided.' Adversarial counsel, independently: 'the cart's hour is a CONSTANT, and a constant explains nothing on n = 2. Both houses shut at eight. There is zero variation in cart hour across the sample, so nothing in this evidence could distinguish the cart governs volume from the cart is irrelevant and something else produces near-parity. To test D you would need a receiving house that shut at a different hour, and the passage does not have one.' Counsel also named an unexcluded rival the passage itself supplies: 'the chandler's flap wanted a new spring. A stiff or ill-hanging hatch across a whole quarter is a plausible depressant on the chandler's count - which would mean his shortfall is mechanical, not temporal.'
findings.why: Recorded but NOT a refutation, for reasons this audit weighs as decisive. The stem asks what is IMPLIED, and in this corpus that licenses the best available inference rather than entailment; every rival option is affirmatively defeated (B by an arithmetic the passage supplies on purpose, C by a sentence that contradicts it outright, A by an imputed motive plus its own counterexample); and the one rival cause counsel found - the flap spring - if operative would mean the chandler's true count was HIGHER, which pushes toward B, an option independently dead on magnitude, so it creates no second defensible answer. Counsel, ruling as judge with all of this in view, still returned D DEFENSIBLE and the item single-answerable. NO REPAIR RECOMMENDED. Counsel's own suggested softening ('the hour of the cart, rather than the length of opening, seems to have shaped what a hatch took') would change student-facing text, would require a fresh G-KEY / G-STEM / G-ENG pass, and would ADD a hedge to the key - which would break the hedge map that currently puts the only qualified surface on a distractor and makes 'pick the moderate answer' score zero. The cure is worse than the complaint.

findings.claim: residue_note describes the surveyor's flap-spring coda as deliberate loose material that 'points at no option'. It in fact points weakly AGAINST the key, which is a better law-9 result than claimed but a less accurate description.
findings.evidence: residue_note: 'The last is deliberate loose material - the office that held the figures noticed a broken spring and not the pattern the figures make - and it points at no option; the passage ends on it and stops rather than resolving (law 9).' Adversarial counsel, given no key and instructed to attack whichever option it judged correct, identified the same sentence as 'live ammunition against D': 'A stiff or ill-hanging hatch across a whole quarter is a plausible depressant on the chandler's count - which would mean his shortfall is mechanical, not temporal.' Counsel also, independently and in the other direction, used the coda as a defeater for option A: 'the one person positioned to call the hours excessive raises nothing about them. A reads a scandal into a document whose own inspector found none.'

Net effect on the item is nil, which is what residue_note was reaching for, and law 9 holds either way. The finding is descriptive precision only: the coda is not inert, it is bidirectionally live, and calling it inert understates how well it is doing its job. Recorded because it is the kind of sentence a future generator will copy on the strength of the note's description rather than the sentence's actual behaviour.

findings.claim: Option B uses a superlative for an explicitly two-member comparison set. One of three G-ENG round-2 votes flagged it; this audit finds the flag technically right, editorially marginal, and harmless in its tell direction.
findings.evidence: Option B: 'The shop that kept its hatch open longest took in far more letters than the other.' G-ENG r2 vote 3, minor: 'class 3/4: house-style usage - the comparison set is explicitly two ("than the other"), and serious-magazine style guides (Economist among them) require the comparative, not the superlative, with two items; editor's rewrite: "The shop that kept its hatch open longer took in far more letters than the other."' Votes 1 and 2 returned pass with zero findings, as did all three G-ENG round-1 votes on the same string (B was not touched by the repair).
findings.why: The prescriptive rule is real and the flag correctly identifies that 'than the other' fixes the set at two. Against it: superlative-for-two is unmarked in contemporary edited BrE, the construction here is a restrictive relative identifying one member of a set rather than a direct two-way comparison, and 5 of 6 G-ENG votes across two rounds saw nothing. Tell direction is benign and worth stating explicitly, since a usage wrinkle confined to one option is the shape that can leak: the wrinkle sits on B, a distractor already dead on the arithmetic, so a solver who down-weights B for its register loses nothing and gains nothing. NO REPAIR RECOMMENDED - 'longer' would also weaken B's over-claiming surface, which is the trap's whole point.

findings.claim: The passage marks the meridiem for two of its three clock times and not for the third, and the item's whole arithmetic rests on the unmarked one.
findings.evidence: 'opened at seven in the morning' (marked), 'when the evening cart went at eight' (marked by 'evening'), 'the bookseller's opened at two' (unmarked). The six-hour span the key needs requires reading 'two' as 2 p.m.
findings.why: Not a defect. The reading is forced by context - a shop hatch, opening before an eight o'clock evening close, in a sequence that has already fixed morning and evening - and all three independent reads took 2 p.m. without hesitation or comment. Recorded because the unmarked time is load-bearing and a future editor should not 'tidy' the marked ones into consistency: spelling out 'two in the afternoon' would numeralise nothing but would flatten the deliberate register variation law 15 is credited with here, and marking all three would make the arithmetic look pre-chewed.

audit_note: Verdict CONFIRMED_NOTES, not REFUTED. The prime directive was to refute and the refutation failed on content at every point that matters: key D is right and uniquely defensible on three independent uncontaminated reads, the arithmetic chain is exact end to end with no computed figure anywhere in the unit that could be wrong, option C's refutation is an entailment rather than an inference, option A is ARGUABLE and no more, every declared statistic reproduces on the shipping bytes, the repair touched exactly what it claims and desynced nothing, and the law-12 append-forward correction is the honest article - false clause preserved verbatim, error diagnosed, family membership conceded, surviving argument restated and explicitly limited, residue booked forward. Law 16 re-verified independently on all three legs with passing controls and both coinages are clear to ship. Where the refutation succeeds is on channel rather than content, and it succeeds harder than the gates recorded. An uncontaminated blind solver given the stem and four options with NO passage returned D at a calibrated 62% against a 25% floor, refused in terms to call the sheet random, and named the mechanism the two G-STEM rounds had circled: three of four options live inside the premise that opening length drives volume and D is the sole denier, so the adjudicating option is the key. The passage-based cold solver, asked separately, also reached D blind and volunteered that the convergence was the finding. Two things sharpen this beyond the usual PARTIALLY note. First, 62% is better than the 1-in-2 blind floor the batch's own inherited efterhandstillagg names as the tolerance line - analogically, since that rule is scoped to stance skew in opinion passages, which is why it belongs with the owner and not with a gate. Second, the fleet-repair-1 change that produced this sheet was made to close a blind channel and made it worse: it retired a two-option contradictory pair and installed a three-against-one shared-presupposition cluster, which G-STEM r2 named at the time ('the repair trading an axis imbalance for a shared-presupposition cluster') and which this audit has now measured. Working the other way, and recorded because it cuts against the charge: the 'X, not Y' surface shape that the blind solver called its strongest single cue is provably not a tell in the corpus a Swedish student is trained on - measured here at 0.74% of authentic ELF keys against 0.68% of authentic distractors - so the leak runs through structure and through an LLM-flavoured heuristic, not through anything HP itself teaches. And the repair history shows this defect relocates rather than resolves; the one repair that would restore option balance requires touching A, which two G-DISTRACTOR rounds have found ARGUABLE and which the repairer correctly declined to gamble on promoting to DEFENSIBLE. The honest choices are to ship with the channel disclosed or to retire the item, and that is the owner's call. Two lesser findings are recorded loudly because they are repeats the pipeline has not learned from. originality_note again asserts neighbour distances it did not compute - here certifying that the nearest real places to 'Draystow' are 'each at edit distance 4' when Drayton sits at 2 and Market Drayton is a Shropshire market town, the passage's own category - which is the same enumeration gap V-FINAL charged one batch earlier against 'Stintbury'/Saintbury, milder by one distance step and with the blocking test still passing. And residue_note again declares untested a detail the rationale then uses as load-bearing (the two shops facing each other across the market place, which is documented fact (iv) under the key), making this the third consecutive batch in which this lane has shipped that contradiction after two audits charged it.
